title: School
label: ch:ml-school
canDo: I can name a school and what happens in it — the lesson, the exam, and the marks.

payoff.summary: From cold: four school words, the three places they came from, and which one changes under a case ending.
payoff.note: FOUR NEW WORDS, AND THE POINT'S NOTE WAS PARTLY STALE. It said 'none of paLLikkoodam, paadam or pareeksha is taught', which is true of those three words and leaves out that the DOMAIN already has anchors: ML-C48-teacher (1290) owns adhyaapakan and ML-C48-student (1300) owns vidyaarthi. So the learner has had the PEOPLE since 1290 with nothing around them, and this chapter supplies the place, the thing taught in it, the test of it and the number at the end. That framing is the chapter's spine and it came out of verifying the note rather than scoping from it. A GLYPH CLAIM WAS CHECKED AGAINST DATA AND AGAINST THE FONT, NOT AGAINST A NOTE. pareeksha needs the ksha conjunct, and ML-A1-SCR-12's note lists 'sha (14)' among nine characters the corpus never teaches -- which would have made this word add script debt. It does not: ML-S121-letter-ssa (471) TEACHES the retroflex sha at U+0D37, and SCR-12's 'sha' is the OTHER sibilant, U+0D36, which really is untaught and which 12 distinct TOKENS in headword position need (sari, pashu, aakaasham among them) across 15 headword fields -- tokens and fields are different numbers here because two of those tokens sit inside multi-word headwords, and SCR-12's own '14' is a third number nobody has re-derived. Filed as HL-C407; not widened into here. Separately paaThaM needs U+0D20, a character NO headword in the corpus has ever used, so the NotoSansMalayalam cmap was read directly before the word was committed to -- present -- which is what lessons.d means by 'a character no book has rendered before is invisible to every local gate'. ROMANIZATIONS ARE COPIED FROM NAMED WITNESSES, NEVER GUESSED: ksha -> ksa from six unanimous headwords (ML-C09, ML-C49, ML-C53, ML-C63, ML-C65, ML-C92), with apEksha fixing the word-final -ksa; the chillu r before a consonant -> r from seven (sharkkara, cherkkuka, karshakan, bharttaavu, karkkatakam, tiirccayaayum, vidyaarthi). Only ThaM is DERIVED rather than copied, because U+0D20 has no witness at all: ta is t, and every aspirate in this corpus carries an h (bha -> bh, dha -> dh), so Tha -> Th. THE TWO SANSKRIT WORDS DELIBERATELY DISAGREE. paaThaM ends in the anusvara and gives way to -tth- under a case ending, exactly as HL-C400 narrowed that rule to say; pareeksha ends in a and does not. Same chapter, same subject, same source language, different endings -- and the chapter says outright that the ENDING decides, not the meaning. That is a revisit of ML-GRAMMAR-C83-OBLIQUE-AM-01 on a word that earns it, rather than a restatement. THE ETYMOLOGY IS GIVEN IN ROMANIZATION ONLY. paLLikkooTaM is palli plus kooTaM, and neither part is a taught headword; naming them in SCRIPT would introduce two unowned tokens, which is the trap lessons.d records as 'the parts a lesson names to explain a word are forward references too'. They are given as palli and kooTaM, the way ML-C10-azhcha gives its Tamil comparisons. The historical claim is hedged to what is checkable about MODERN Malayalam -- palli is the word for a mosque or a church, kooTaM is a hall -- with the why offered as the traditional account rather than asserted.
